content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade for the Apple assistant, now available on iOS 27. I noticed a standout difference between it and other AI assistants, and it's a good difference.

The new Siri on iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, which is completely different from other AI chatbots

Since the first beta of iOS 27 was released, I've been using Siri AI for almost four months. Overall, it has delivered everything I expected from it.

The new Siri is much better than the previous generation, truly fulfilling the original promise of a capable assistant on Apple devices.

I'll admit that if you need the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tools, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be a better fit for you.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it with those third-party tools, I found one key difference that made me prefer Siri more.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't drone on, mimic human personalities, or try to get you to develop a personal relationship with it.

Siri is helpful and smart, doing whatever you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It will frequently remind you that it's an AI, so it might make mistakes. And it won't pretend to be in a relationship with you.

On the other hand, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality and opinions, displaying more human-like tendencies, which feel very fake to me.

I think some users prefer that more 'humanised' approach. But I'd rather have AI assistants stick to doing their job, without pretending to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has designed the new Siri accordingly.

How 'human-like' do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
